name: Familial Congenital Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnosis of Familial Congenital Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction

criteria.description: Persistent tearing (epiphora) from birth or early infancy
Mucopurulent discharge from the affected eye(s)
Delayed or absent drainage on fluorescein dye disappearance test
Documented family history of congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction
Imaging evidence of nasolacrimal duct obstruction on dacryocystography

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent epiphora and mucopurulent discharge from birth with positive fluorescein dye disappearance test
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by family history and imaging when available.

pathognomonic.notes: Continuous tearing due to obstruction of nasolacrimal duct
Sticky discharge often present due to tear stasis and secondary infection

common.notes: Episodes of conjunctivitis secondary to tear duct obstruction

common.symptomName: Swelling over the lacrimal sac area
common.notes: Mild swelling due to tear accumulation

searchTerms: delayed dye clearance in eye test

common.symptomName: Positive family history of nasolacrimal duct obstruction
searchTerms: family history of blocked tear ducts

occasional.notes: Infection of lacrimal sac due to obstruction
May be present due to associated nasal mucosal swelling

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial discomfort near lacrimal sac
occasional.notes: Due to tear stasis and inflammation

rare.symptomName: Fistula formation from lacrimal sac to skin
searchTerms: abnormal tear duct opening on skin

laboratory: Culture of lacrimal sac discharge may reveal bacterial pathogens in secondary infection
imaging: Dacryocystography showing obstruction at the distal nasolacrimal duct
Ultrasound of lacrimal sac demonstrating fluid retention
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern suggesting autosomal dominant or recessive transmission
other: Positive fluorescein dye disappearance test indicating impaired tear drainage

distinguishingFeatures: Cystic swelling over lacrimal sac present at birth
May cause respiratory distress in neonates

redFlags: Acute dacryocystitis with pain, redness, and swelling
Fistula formation from lacrimal sac to skin
Failure to resolve with conservative management beyond 12 months
references: Orphanet: Familial congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction - ORPHA:451612
American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern: Epiphora and Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction
